newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait's bourse hits record highs in week.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait's bourse hits record highs in week.

text.p: Volume, value and the index hit record highs on Kuwait's bourse in the week to Wednesday and dealers said market confidence attracted capital from abroad.
"The market is attracting investors from (other) Gulf states," said Mohammad al-Duhaishi, a private dealer.

Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Kuwait's foreign residents are allowed to take part in mutual funds run by Kuwaiti firms.
The index closed at 1,747 points, a rise of 60.2 points or 3.5 percent from last week's 1,686.8 points record.
Traded value gained 63 percent to 296.5 million dinars ($991.6 million), a daily average of 59.6 million dinars.
Volume rose 65 percent to 1.506 billion shares, a daily average of 301.2 million. Trade opens daily for two-and-a-half hours. Gainers led losers 37-7 and 10 shares were non-movers.
"Some foreign companies are trying to enter the market through mutual funds," said Khaled al-Saleh, chairman of Gulf Brokerage Company.
Kuwait is considering opening trade to foreign investors.
Officials say trade picked up due to good indicators such as a decline in the budget gap and confidence in security.
On Tuesday, Parliament approved a 4.21 billion dinar budget with a projected net deficit of 1.21 billion for the July-June fiscal year. Last year's deficit was estimated at 1.32 billion.
Other positive factors included progress by the government in settling the principle on a $5.5 billion sovereign loan.
Some experts expect a correction to hit the property and investments sectors, slightly pulling the strong banking sector down.
The most active stocks were Commercial Bank, Investment Projects, United Realty, Pearl of Kuwait Real Estate and Kuwait Real Estate.

Property firms were the most active sector by value with 31.4 percent, followed by investment shares with 25.5 percent and banks with 23 percent. Properties were the most active by volume with 33 percent. Investment firms came second with 31.5 percent and banks third with 30.2 percent.
